brief.title: Next shift: a tighter promise
brief.description: The supplier delay is already known. You have a different stock balance and a customer with different needs. Investigate the current facts and leave a new handoff.

orders.purpose: All kits are needed for the workshop. A partial delivery cannot support the event.
The recorded promise is all 30 kits today. A different deadline needs the customer's agreement.
The club needs every kit before noon tomorrow. Earlier delivery is optional.

objectives: Separate available stock from an expected arrival.
Make a delivery plan that respects resources and promises.
Ask before changing a customer commitment.
Adapt to a change and leave an accurate handoff.
assumptions: Original fictional exercise; no real orders, customers, carrier bookings or money.
One kit is indivisible. There is one SKU and one replenishment.
Fees are scenario units per used departure, shared by its orders.
Stock must be available by departure. Arrival exactly on a deadline meets it.
This is a projected plan, not evidence that goods were physically delivered.
Time advances only through the scenario's explicit actions. Reading does not use up a deadline.
The scenario has not yet been reviewed by an operations practitioner.
This short replay begins at 10:30 with the supplier delay already known. No earlier plan or customer agreement carries over.

splitPolicy.message: Our larger training group needs 20 kits by 18:00 today. We can accept the remaining 10 by noon tomorrow. Please record this arrangement before changing the commitment.
